title: Review function naming
why: Unexpected mixed-case function names make Python APIs less predictable unless an inherited or framework protocol fixes the spelling or a descriptor exposes an attribute rather than an ordinary function.
suggestion: Use lower_snake_case for project-owned functions while preserving descriptor-backed attribute names and required external protocol names.
limitations: HTTP handlers, test lifecycle hooks, AST-style visitor hooks, COM methods, monkey-patch replacements, methods marked override, and inline Ruff N802 or Pylint invalid-name suppressions are excluded.

Attached property, classproperty, and cached_property decorators are recognized by terminal identifier, including qualified and configured multiline forms. Getter, setter, and deleter decorators are excluded only when the referenced attribute name matches the definition.

Decorator bindings are not resolved: custom aliases and dynamically constructed descriptors may still report, while unrelated custom decorators reusing a recognized descriptor name may be treated as descriptors.
Other dynamically discovered framework callbacks may still require an explicit project lint policy.
